title: Blackfathom Deeps
body: Blackfathom Deeps opens at the northern end of the Zoram Strand, where the forest of Ashenvale meets the sea. It was once a temple of the night elves' moon goddess, Elune, until the Sundering shattered it and sank it beneath the waves. For ages its drowned halls lay undisturbed, until the naga and the satyrs came, drawn by its ancient power. Now Blindlight murlocs crowd the halls nearest the entrance, Blackfathom sea witches and myrmidons hold the great pools beyond, and Fallenroot satyrs stalk the tunnels. The cultists have gathered deeper in, among the ruins of an old shrine, crying that the Old Gods will be restored and that Aku'mai demands more sacrifices. Legend holds that an ancient beast of that name, a favored pet of the Old Gods, has made its lair in the temple's depths. The Argent Dawn and the Earthen Ring both have business with the cult here, and a collector of old lore wants a manuscript said to lie at the bottom.

title: The Pool of Ask'ar
body: The Pool of Ask'ar is the first great flooded hall of the deeps, a wide basin of dark water beyond the passages where the murlocs dwell. Blackfathom sea witches and myrmidons keep watch around it, crustaceans scuttle through its shallows, and in the pool itself swims Ghamoo-ra, a sea turtle of great size. Off the pool a side cavern opens, and there a naga called Lady Sarevess holds her ground with a myrmidon of her people at her side.

title: The Shrine of Gelihast
body: Some way into the deeps, past the first halls, Blindlight murlocs, oracles and muckdwellers have gathered around an old shrine of the drowned temple. Their master is Gelihast, a hulking murloc larger than any of his kin, and the shrine is his: his followers crowd close about it and let no stranger near. The stone stands dark and silent among them. What the shrine once was, and whom it honored, no one has said.

title: The Moonshrine Ruins
body: Deep within the flooded temple lie the Moonshrine Ruins, the broken remains of a shrine of the moon, half drowned in dark water. The Twilight's Hammer has made its camp among them. Acolytes tend the wounded, reavers swing heavy blows, loreseekers swell and slow their foes, and aquamancers keep elementals of living water at their sides, while the cult's cries that the Old Gods will be restored echo off the old stones.

title: The Forgotten Pool
body: Below the cult's sanctum lies the Forgotten Pool, a deep basin of black water at the heart of the drowned temple. Threshfins hunt in its depths and barbed crustaceans crawl along its edges, but the pool has an older master. Old Serra'kis, a great thresher, glides through the dark water beneath the cultists' feet, and whoever swims these waters swims through his.

title: Twilight Lord Kelris
body: Twilight Lord Kelris leads the Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps. An orc, he keeps to the Moonshrine Sanctum above the Forgotten Pool, where he sits deep in meditation, channeling dark power, while shadowmages and elementalists of the cult stand watch around him. Four great braziers, the Fires of Aku'mai, stand about the sanctum, and beyond them a massive portal holds shut the way deeper into the temple. Every cultist who cries that Aku'mai demands more sacrifices answers to him.

title: Aku'mai
body: Aku'mai is the beast the Twilight's Hammer reveres in Blackfathom Deeps. Legend holds that it is an ancient creature, a favored pet of the Old Gods, that has taken up residence in the ruins of the temple and preyed upon the area ever since, and the cult has gathered here to be near it. Its name is on every cultist's lips: Aku'mai demands more sacrifices, they cry. Its lair lies somewhere beyond the sealed portal that bears its name. How it came to the temple is a tale the Argent Dawn can tell.
sources: the pre-Cataclysm official description (legends hold the ancient beast Aku'mai, a favored pet of the primordial Old Gods, has taken up residence within the temple's ruins and preyed upon the area ever since; the Twilight's Hammer drawn to its presence); warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Blackfathom_Deeps_(Classic) (the cult guards Aku'mai, a pet of the Old Gods)

parts.body: The way to Aku'mai opened only once the four Fires of Aku'mai in the sanctum were lit. Each fire called up defenders: snapping turtles, crustaceans and servants of living water that rained frost. When the last of them died, the great portal opened. Beyond it, past more of the turtles, the beast waited in its pool, a hydra of terrible size. Aku'mai fought wrapped in a cloud of poison and flew into frenzied rages, but at last it lay dead.

He had once followed the Twilight's Hammer, he said, and come here to draw power from the cursed beast, but the sacrifice of countless innocents brought him to his senses. Trapped so far from his homeland of Khaz Modan, he was free now, and he offered his rescuers passage to Darnassus.

title: Baron Aquanis
body: Baron Aquanis is a water elemental of the Moonshrine Ruins, a great form of living water. He keeps no watch where he can be seen. When the fathom stone that lies in the water of the ruins is disturbed, he rises from the depths and emerges to protect it, and whoever has laid hands on the stone must answer to him.

title: Knowledge in the Deeps
body: In the Forlorn Cavern of Ironforge, Gerrig Bonegrip gathers lore, and not the harmless kind: the old and powerful sort said to open doorways and stir Those Who Sleep. Now he has heard rumors of an old piece of it, the Lorgalis Manuscript, said to lie at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps. That place, he says, was the dwelling of long-dead elves who held great knowledge before their city fell to ruin. He wants the manuscript found and brought to him, and whoever does it, he promises, will not be forgotten, not even after the end days.

title: The Orb of Soran'ruk
body: In the southern Barrens, Doan Karhan knows the orbs of the Burning Legion well. When a demon falls out of the Legion's favor, he explains, its spirit is imprisoned within an orb and handed to the Legion's mages and warlocks, and many such orbs were carried into Azeroth by their servants. Even broken, they keep the powers of the demons inside. The orb of Soran'ruk was split in two. One half was broken again, its fragments carried by the acolytes of the Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps; the larger piece lies in Shadowfang Keep. Bring him the pieces, and he can make the orb whole.

Three of its four pieces come from Blackfathom's acolytes, so the story sits here; Shadowfang is named only as where the larger piece lies. The quest calls its holder a wizard, but it drops from a worgen (Shadowfang Darksoul), so the opening does not say who holds it. His life's study of the orbs is his reward text, so the opening says only that he knows them. Faction 0 (AllowableRaces 0; Doan is neutral). Opening on ACCEPT 1740, part on DONE 1740.

parts.body: The pieces came back to Doan, and the orb proved hardly broken at all: almost every fragment was there, and making Soran'ruk whole was a simple thing for one who had spent his life on such work. He was glad of the chance to study the pieces, and handed the orb back reforged in whatever form its bearer chose. His own orb, Zargain, had taken him many years to gather.
sources: quest 1740 reward text (the orb was not greatly fragmented, almost all of the pieces are here; a simple thing to recreate them; I will give them back fully reconstructed in a form of your choosing) and request text (it took me many years to collect the pieces of the orb of Zargain); RewardChoiceItem 6898 Orb of Soran'ruk, 15109 Staff of Soran'ruk
